ai.literal: Truthfulness, that which is called, what if asked: whatever even one harm without speaking.
ai.translation: If asked what is called truthfulness, it is the speaking of words that are free from even the slightest harm.
ai.modern: வாய்மை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எது என்று கேட்டால், அது மற்றவருக்குச் சிறிதளவும் தீங்கு தராத சொற்களைச் சொல்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines truthfulness (வாய்மை) by focusing on its effect rather than mere factual accuracy. If asked what truthfulness is, the answer is speaking words that carry no harm (தீமை இலாத). The combination of 'யாது' and 'ஒன்றும்' stresses that not even the slightest harm should be caused by what is said. Therefore, true speech is fundamentally harmless speech.

ai.literal: Even falsehood has the place of truth, if it yields goodness free from flaw.
ai.translation: Even falsehood takes the place of truth, if it produces a flawless good.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்ற நன்மையை உருவாக்குமானால், பொய்யான சொல்லும் உண்மையாகவே கருதப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines truthfulness not just by factual accuracy, but by its ultimate moral effect. It states that even a false statement can be elevated to the status of truth. This happens only if the falsehood results in a pure, flawless benefit for others. The key word 'புரைதீர்ந்த' (flawless) ensures that the outcome must be entirely good, without any hidden harm.

ai.literal: One's own heart that which is known let one not lie; lied after, one's own heart itself oneself will burn.
ai.translation: Do not lie about what your own heart knows to be true. If you do, your own heart will burn you.
ai.modern: தன் நெஞ்சுக்குத் தெரிந்த உண்மையை மறைத்துப் பொய் சொல்லக் கூடாது. அப்படிப் பொய் சொன்னால், தன் நெஞ்சமே தன்னைத் தண்டித்து வருத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the inescapable internal consequence of speaking a falsehood. The phrase 'தன் நெஞ்சு அறிவது' refers to the truth that a person is fully aware of in their own mind. If one speaks against this inner knowledge, the resulting guilt cannot be avoided. The word 'சுடும்' (will burn) vividly captures how one's own conscience becomes the punisher, inflicting mental agony after the lie is told.

ai.literal: With the mind without lying if one conducts oneself, of the people of the world in the minds all he is.
ai.translation: If one lives without falsehood in one's own heart, one will live in the hearts of all people in the world.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் மனத்திற்குத் தெரிந்து பொய் சொல்லாமல் நேர்மையாக வாழ்ந்தால், அவன் உலக மக்களின் உள்ளங்களில் எல்லாம் நிலைத்து நிற்பான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of absolute truthfulness. If a person conducts their life without any falsehood even in their own mind ('உள்ளத்தால் பொய்யாது ஒழுகின்'), they achieve a lasting place in the hearts of everyone ('உலகத்தார் உள்ளத்துள் எல்லாம் உளன்'). True honesty is not just in words but in one's innermost thoughts. Such inner purity naturally commands universal respect and endears the person to the whole world.

ai.literal: With the mind truthfulness if speaks, penance with charity than those who do, chief.
ai.translation: If one speaks the truth from the heart, one is superior to those who perform penance and give to charity.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் மனத்தோடு பொருந்திய உண்மையைச் சொல்வானானால், அவன் தவமும் தானமும் செய்பவர்களை விடச் சிறந்தவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the virtue of truthfulness to the traditional virtues of penance and charity. The phrase 'maṉattoṭu' emphasizes that truth must be spoken from the heart, aligning one's words completely with one's inner thoughts. If a person achieves this sincere truthfulness, the text states they are 'talai' (the head or superior) compared to those who merely perform outward acts of asceticism and charity. Thus, inner honesty is elevated above all other righteous deeds.

ai.literal: Non-lying like fame there is not; without weariness all virtues it will give.
ai.translation: There is no fame like that of never lying. Without any further effort, it will yield every other virtue.
ai.modern: பொய் சொல்லாமல் இருப்பதைப் போன்ற சிறந்த புகழ் வேறு இல்லை. அது ஒருவருக்கு எந்தச் சிரமமும் இல்லாமல் மற்ற எல்லா அறங்களையும் கொடுக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of truthfulness among all virtues. The word 'பொய்யாமை' means the practice of never telling a lie, which is described as the greatest source of fame. The term 'எய்யாமை' means without weariness or effort. The poet explains that simply maintaining truthfulness will automatically and effortlessly bring the benefits of all other moral virtues to a person.

ai.literal: Not lying, not lying if performed, virtue other not doing, not doing is good.
ai.translation: If one strictly practices the single virtue of never lying, it is perfectly fine to not practice any other virtues.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் பொய் சொல்லாமையை மட்டுமே உறுதியாகக் கடைப்பிடித்தால், அவன் வேறு எந்த அறச் செயல்களையும் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே அவனுக்குப் போதுமான நன்மையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute supremacy of truthfulness over all other moral acts. By repeating the words for 'not lying' (பொய்யாமை) and 'not doing' (செய்யாமை), the poet creates a powerful emphasis. It means that if one flawlessly adheres to the single principle of never telling a lie, that alone is enough. The strict practice of truthfulness makes the performance of other virtues unnecessary, as it inherently contains all moral goodness.

ai.literal: Outside purity by water is achieved; inside purity by truthfulness will be seen.
ai.translation: Purity of the body is achieved with water, but purity of the mind is revealed through truthfulness.
ai.modern: உடலின் புறத்தூய்மை நீரினால் ஏற்படும்; ஆனால் உள்ளத்தின் அகத்தூய்மை ஒருவனது வாய்மையால் மட்டுமே அறியப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical cleanliness with inner purity. While the outside of the body can be washed and made clean with water, the purity of the mind cannot be cleansed physically. Instead, inner purity is achieved and made visible to others only through truthfulness. The phrase 'காணப்படும்' (will be seen) emphasizes that true inner purity naturally reveals itself through a person's honest words and actions.

ai.literal: All lamps lamps are not; to the noble ones unfailing lamp indeed lamp.
ai.translation: Not all lamps are true lamps; to the noble, the lamp of truth is the only lamp.
ai.modern: உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லா விளக்குகளும் உண்மையான விளக்குகள் ஆகா. சான்றோர்களுக்குப் பொய் சொல்லாமை என்னும் விளக்கே உண்மையான விளக்கு ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet distinguishes between physical light and moral light. While ordinary lamps dispel physical darkness, they are not considered true lamps by the wise. To the noble ones, the unfailing lamp of truthfulness is the only real lamp, as it dispels the darkness of ignorance and deceit. The repetition of the word lamp emphasizes the superiority of inner truth over outer illumination.

ai.literal: Among those we have seen as truth, there is not anything whatsoever, good things other than truthfulness.
ai.translation: Among all the things we have realized as true, there is nothing whatsoever that is better than truthfulness.
ai.modern: நாம் உண்மையாக உணர்ந்தவற்றுள், வாய்மையை விடச் சிறந்த வேறு நல்ல பொருள்கள் சிறிதளவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The poet speaks from collective experience, stating that among all the things recognized as true or real, nothing surpasses truthfulness. The word வாய்மையின் uses the comparative suffix இன் to weigh truthfulness against all other virtues. Consequently, no other good thing, no matter how small, can be considered greater than being truthful.
